'''Wolfgang Krätschmer''' (born 16 November 1942 in [[Berlin]]) is a German physicist.

Krätschmer studied physics in Berlin. After his [[Diplom]] he went to the [[Max Planck Institute for Nuclear Physics]] in [[Heidelberg]] and earned his PhD there in 1971 with a thesis on artificially etched tracks of accelerated heavy ions in [[quartz]]. In his career, he has worked on cosmic-ray heavy-ion tracks in [[moon rock|lunar samples]], as well as infrared and UV spectra of [[cosmic dust|interstellar dust]].

Together with his PhD student [[Konstantinos Fostiropoulos]] and with [[Donald Huffman]] from the [[University of Arizona]], he developed a procedure<ref>Krätschmer, Fostiropoulos, Huffman: "Search for the UV and IR spectra of C60 in laboratory-produced carbon dust", [https://www.springer.com/us/book/9780792308638# Dusty Objects in the Universe, September 1989, Capri, Italy"], conference proceedings, page 89-93</ref><ref name=Kroto1993>{{Cite book| author=Krätschmer & Huffman |editor1=Kroto, H. W. |editor2=Walton, D. R. M. | chapter = Production and discovery of fullerites: new forms of crystalline carbon | title = Fullerenes| publisher = Cambridge U. Press | year = 1993 | pages = 33–38 | isbn = 0-521-45917-6 | chapter-url = https://books.google.com/books?isbn=0521459176&pg=PA33}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal| author=Wolfgang Krätschmer| title=The story of making fullerenes | journal=Nanoscale|volume=3| issue=6 |year=2011|pages=2485–2489|doi=10.1039/C0NR00925C| pmid=21327257 | bibcode=2011Nanos...3.2485K }}</ref> for the synthesis of [[fullerene]]s. This procedure was the first to produce [[Konstantinos Fostiropoulos#The Heidelberg experiments|fullerenes in large amounts]] for chemical experiments. Since 1993, he is an honorary professor ("Honorarprofessor") at the [[University of Heidelberg]].

==Honors==
* 1992 – [[Stern–Gerlach Medal]]
* 1993 – [[Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Prize]]
* 1994 – Hewlett-Packard Europhysics Prize
* 2002 – [[Carl Friedrich Gauss Medaille]]
* 2008 – [[Liebig Medal]]
* 2008 – Honorary doctorate from the [[University of Basel]]
* 2010 – [[European Inventor Award]] in the "Lifetime Achievement" category<ref>[http://www.epo.org/learning-events/european-inventor/finalists/2010/kraetschmer.html Invention: Process for working with new form of carbon]</ref> awarded by the [[European Patent Office]]
